blueprints.primary_construct: Explain a process with a clear opening, connected development, relevant detail, and ending
blueprints.prompt_text: Your student club is planning a small welcome event. Explain to a new volunteer how to organize it: introduce the aim, describe two or three steps with relevant details, and finish with a clear summary. Prepare silently for 60 seconds, then speak for 45 to 60 seconds. Give your first answer without hints, a model, or feedback.

criteria.description: Connects ordered steps and relevant details
Ends with a clear summary or recommendation

semantic_scope.acceptable_variants: Any realistic process that addresses the assigned situation

blueprints.primary_construct: Track one speaker's concern and identify how the second speaker responds
blueprints.prompt_text: This is consolidation using a previously heard dialogue, so it is training evidence only. Listen again without the transcript. Explain Mia's concern and how Leo's response addresses it.

material.transcript_text: Mia: I know the optional research workshop could help, but it meets on Friday afternoon, when I usually finish my lab reports. I am not sure the benefit is worth losing that time. Leo: That makes sense. Why not attend the first meeting and ask whether later sessions are recorded? Then you can judge the value without committing every Friday.

criteria.description: Identifies the time conflict and Mia's uncertainty about whether the benefit is worth it
Explains that Leo validates the concern and proposes a trial before commitment

required_meaning_units: Friday workshop conflicts with lab-report time
Mia is unsure about the tradeoff
Leo proposes attending once and checking recordings before deciding
semantic_scope.acceptable_variants: Any wording that preserves the concern-response relationship
invalid_conditions: states only isolated details without the relationship

blueprints.primary_construct: Explain a process with a clear opening, connected development, relevant detail, and ending
blueprints.prompt_text: A classmate is finding it difficult to balance a part-time job and coursework. Explain a practical weekly planning routine, using a clear opening, ordered steps with details, and a brief conclusion. Prepare for 45 to 60 seconds and speak for 45 to 60 seconds.

criteria.description: Connects ordered steps and relevant details
Ends with a clear summary or recommendation

semantic_scope.acceptable_variants: Any realistic process that addresses the assigned situation

blueprints.primary_construct: Identify an expository text's main line and explain how a detail supports it
blueprints.prompt_text: Read the passage. Identify its problem–trial–evidence–conclusion structure. Explain how the return-rate detail supports the proposed improvement, and state one limit on the conclusion.

material.text: A university library tested a new system for lending chargers. Under the old system, students could borrow one for a whole day, but many chargers were unavailable by lunchtime. The library then introduced two-hour loans and a reminder sent fifteen minutes before the return time. During the four-week trial, more students were able to borrow chargers in the afternoon. However, late returns remained common on days when the reminder service failed. Staff suggested keeping the shorter loan period and improving the reliability of the reminders. They also noted that the trial took place outside the examination season. Demand may be higher during exams, so the results do not yet show whether the same system will work equally well throughout the year.

criteria.description: Identifies the shortage, trial, results and qualified recommendation
Connects failed reminders to late returns and explains the exam-season limitation

required_meaning_units: reminder failures coincided with late returns
invalid_conditions: reverses the relation between reminders and returns

blueprints.primary_construct: Explain a workable group coordination process
blueprints.prompt_text: In about 80 words, explain how students can coordinate a group assignment when their schedules differ. Give a practical method, explain its steps, and say why it helps.

criteria.description: Explains ordered steps and why they help
Uses understandable sentence boundaries and links

semantic_scope.acceptable_variants: Any realistic method for coordinating different schedules
